ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, as amended and in force, together with its Executive Regulations issued under Prime Ministerial Decree No. 212 of 2002, as amended; beneficial-ownership registration and record-keeping obligations under the Commercial Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 and the applicable GAFI and Commercial Registry implementing decisions; Central Bank of Egypt customer-due-diligence instructions for residents opening bank accounts; and directives issued by the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport and civil registry authority of the individual's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular legalization (Egypt is not an Apostille Contracting State; origin-country Ministry of Foreign Affairs or Ministry of Justice certification, followed by Egyptian embassy/consulate legalization, then Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs attestation where required)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing, commercial register extract, or certificate of incorporation and incumbency of any juridical shareholder or corporate director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry in the shareholder's or director's jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular legalization chain; if the origin state is an Apostille party, the apostille is still required to be supplemented by Egyptian consular attestation unless expressly waived by bilateral reciprocity

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney appointing the Egyptian incorporation lawyer or registered agent and specifying the registered-office arrangement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin, authenticated by the Egyptian consular post in that country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular legalization; Arabic notarized translation prepared by an Egyptian licensed translator is mandatory before filing

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution of any foreign corporate shareholder approving the Egyptian LLC incorporation, shareholding, UBO declaration, and signatory authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the foreign corporate shareholder, certified by its corporate secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in the origin country followed by consular legalization for Egypt; certified Arabic translation required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory baseline KYC on all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories before incorporation; mandatory PEP screening of beneficial owners and connected family members/business associates; mandatory screening against OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the Egyptian national counter-terrorism and financial-sanctions lists, and Central Bank of Egypt warnings. Positive PEP/sanctions matches trigger enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds and wealth documentation, senior-management approval, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Routine low-risk classification for this resin-statue business does not exempt the applicant from statutory sanctions screening, and records must be retained for at least five years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) electronic investor-services portal available at www.gafi.gov.eg and the 'Invest in Egypt' online platform, complemented by the Ministry of Trade and Industry's Commercial Registry (Aman) name-conflict check system.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The mandatory legal company name must be in Arabic script; a Latin-script transliteration may be recorded as a trade name only if the Arabic name remains the governing legal name. The name must be consistent with the declared activity, must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing commercial name or registered trademark in Egypt, and must not imply activities for which the company holds no license.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Arab Republic of Egypt / جمهورية مصر العربية
Pharmaceutical or medical terms requiring sectoral licensing
Words contrary to public order or public morals
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Step 1: Upon name rejection, GAFI issues an electronic rejection notice with the legal ground and file reference. Step 2: The applicant files a written Arabic administrative objection with the GAFI One-Stop Shop or through the online portal within 15 working days of rejection, attaching the rejection notice, proposed Arabic name, trademark registration or consent letters, and explanation of distinctiveness. Step 3: The GAFI name-clearance committee issues a decision within 10 working days. Step 4: If the committee refuses, the applicant may appeal to the GAFI chief executive officer within 15 working days. Step 5: Exhaustion of administrative remedies permits judicial review before the Administrative Court of the State Council within 60 days of the final refusal. The initial reservation is not extandable after expiry; a fresh clearance application and fee are required.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is conditionally permissible only when structured as a licensed serviced office with a physical Egyptian address, local mail acceptance, and process-agent service. A pure mail-forwarding virtual mailbox without a physical presence will not satisfy the Commercial Registry, Egyptian Tax Authority, or GAFI requirements. For a resin-statue garage-kit production business, the registered office should coincide with or properly identify the storage and production location, and the company must be able to evidence commercial substance, business records, and accessibility for official service.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: approximately 10% baseline probability of an unannounced GAFI or Commercial Registry physical inspection in the first 12 months. The likelihood increases to 25-35% if the registered office is a pure virtual office, a residential apartment, or unrelated to the declared resin-casting and storage activity. Tax-office inspection risk arises separately after tax-card and VAT registration, with a similar low-to-moderate profile for this non-sensitive manufacturing activity.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended), particularly the LLC provisions and Executive Regulations (Decree No. 96/1982), as integrated with Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and GAFI one-stop shop rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Investment Services Center / Commercial Registry, Ministry of Investment, Egypt.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association (Aqd Al-Ta'sis) in Arabic, notarized and filed electronically through the GAFI one-stop shop.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed on LLCs under Law No. 159/1981; shareholders determine capital in the Articles, and the full nominal value of subscribed shares must be paid into a blocked preliminary account in an Egyptian licensed bank and released only after the issuance of the incorporation certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the share subscriptions set forth in the Memorandum of Association are ratified in full and each founder's subscribed shares are hereby accepted and allotted. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company shall be established at the address stated in the Articles of Association, and the Managers are authorized to execute the lease and to file all statutory notices. RESOLVED, that [Name] and [Name] be and are hereby appointed as Managers, with power to act jointly or severally as permitted, and [Name] is appointed as the officer responsible for tax filings. RESOLVED, that all officers are authorized to complete licensing, open bank accounts, and take all steps necessary for business commencement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Legal Form Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI 'Esal' / Invest in Egypt online one-stop portal; Commercial Registry name database.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register on the GAFI electronic portal, submit three requested corporate names in Arabic, select the LLC legal form, and obtain preliminary approval of the reserved name valid for 90 days.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID copy of each founder/shareholder
Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association in Arabic
Name reservation request form
Certificate of non-conflicting corporate name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, resubmit alternative names within 10 working days or request a reconsideration before the GAFI name committee under the Executive Regulations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization and Legalization of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public Office (Kitabat al-Adl) and GAFI authentication unit.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize the Arabic Memorandum and Articles of Association, have all founders sign in person or by valid power of attorney, and obtain notarial authentication of signatures as required by law.
required_dossiers: Arabic Memorandum and Articles of Association
Valid national ID or passport of each subscriber
Power of attorney if signed by representative
Article of association drafting fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary issues a form query, correct the bylaw articles and re-authenticate; GAFI may also accept an electronic notarization and rectify inconsistencies by written amendment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Deposit and Bank Subscription Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian licensed bank recognized by GAFI for incorporation accounts.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a time-limited blocked preliminary account in the company's name under formation, deposit the fully paid subscribed share capital, and obtain a bank capital deposit certificate evidencing funds availability.
required_dossiers: Founders' national IDs or passports
Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Name reservation certificate
Capital transfer or deposit order in Egyptian Pounds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to issue the capital certificate, reconcile remittance documentation and provide a corrected anti-money laundering declaration; request resubmission through the GAFI-approved bank branch.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI One-Stop Incorporation Submission and Certificate Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Investment Services Center, Cairo or governorate branch.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete incorporation application with annexed notarized by-laws, bank capital certificate, lease or title evidence, and officer appointments through GAFI; pay the official filing fee; GAFI verifies compliance and issues the Certificate of Incorporation and preliminary commercial registry extract.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Bank capital deposit certificate
Registered office lease contract or ownership document
Appointment letter of Managers and tax officer
Copy of name reservation certificate
GAFI fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI raises a query, submit corrective documentation within 30 days through the electronic tracking system; a rejected filing may be cured by amending the by-laws and resubmitting, with further recourse to GAFI's internal reconsideration window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Commercial Registry Completion
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Tax Authority (GTA) and Commercial Registry Directorate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the integrated registration applications to obtain the corporate tax card, prepare VAT registration particulars, complete commercial registry extract issuance, and ensure the company's official incorporation entry in the Commercial Registry.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Notarized Articles of Association
Bank capital certificate and account opening statement
Registered office lease or title evidence
Managers' and tax officer's national IDs
Cancelled official stamp for post-registration recordclients
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the General Tax Authority or Commercial Registry delays issuance, request escalation through the GAFI one-stop shop and file a formal follow-up to obtain the tax card and registry extract within the statutory deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI) and Ministry of Labor offices.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as an employer with NOSI, submit the mandatory payroll and employment contract declarations, and obtain the labor office registration stamps required for lawful hiring.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Corporate tax card
Manager national ID or passport
Standard employment contracts for intended staff
Registered office lease or offic administrative address evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If NOSI raises a payroll or worker classification query, provide corrected declarations, amended salaries lists, and amended shareholding details; if the query persists, escalate to the central NOSI complaints office.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA) in coordination with GAFI One-Stop Investment Services Center and the Industrial Licensing Directorate, Ministry of Trade and Industry.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Industrial Operating License for Small Manufacturing Workshops / Operating License for Polyresin Casting Workshop.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA), Ministry of Environment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B – Initial Environmental Impact Assessment and registration required for small resin casting garage workshop; full EIA Category C is required if resin throughput or hazardous waste volumes exceed the small workshop thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Law No. 4/1994 and its executive regulations: industrial wastewater pH 6–9, TSS ≤ 60 mg/L, COD ≤ 100 mg/L or as required by the receiving sewer authority; VOC emissions from resin mixing and vacuum casting must be controlled with local exhaust ventilation and carbon filtration, with styrene workplace threshold limited to applicable TLV of 50 ppm; uncured resin, contaminated packaging and off-spec castings must be segregated and disposed of through licensed non-hazardous industrial waste handlers; no unpermitted discharge to storm water drains.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense Directorate fire safety certification, structural load inspection of the garage facility, and occupational safety clearance under Law No. 12/2003, including installation of fire extinguishers, proper ventilation, emergency exits, eye-wash and PPE procedures before the industrial operating license is released.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA – مصلحة الضرائب المصرية); unified national tax portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; e-invoicing/e-receipt platform: https://einvoicing.eta.gov.eg; customs export clearance and documentation administered by the Egyptian Customs Authority through the NAFIZA single window: https://www.nafiza.gov.eg.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate the LLC through the General Authority for Investment (GAFI, https://www.gafi.gov.eg) and obtain the Commercial Registration Certificate from the Commercial Registry of the Ministry of Trade and Industry. 2) File the unified tax registration application with ETA within 30 days of registration or commencement of activity, attaching the notarized Articles of Association, commercial registry extract, premises title/lease, and identity documents of owners/managers; ETA then issues a permanent Tax Identification Number (TIN), the unified Tax Card (بطاقة ضريبية) covering income tax, payroll/salary tax, stamp tax and VAT, plus a separate VAT registration certificate under Law 67/2016. 3) Register as an exporter with the Egyptian Customs Authority in NAFIZA and obtain the exporter code/electronic signature. 4) Complete ETA e-invoicing onboarding (XML/JSON API integration or web portal) before issuing the first invoice. 5) Foreign non-resident ownership is permitted with no minimum capital requirement; if the business operates as a branch or permanent establishment of a foreign entity, a local fiscal representative must be appointed for registration, filing and e-invoicing; pure non-resident exporters without Egyptian nexus need only register for Egypt-source withholding obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. Under Income Tax Law 91 of 2005, an Egyptian LLC is a resident juridical person taxed at entity level on worldwide income at the general corporate rate of 22.5%; no pass-through or partnership-style attribution is available. The regime is non-territorial (worldwide income with foreign tax credit relief). The business is not situated in a licensed tax-exempt investment zone (Suez Canal Economic Zone incentives apply only to projects licensed inside that zone), so standard national CIT and VAT rules apply.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not offer check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch elections; an LLC is per se a corporate taxpayer under Law 91/2005 and cannot elect pass-through treatment. Available statutory elections and mechanisms: (i) election of a non-calendar fiscal year subject to ETA approval; (ii) SME simplified presumptive taxation under Law 152/2020 for qualifying businesses with turnover up to EGP 40 million; (iii) foreign tax credit election for foreign-source income instead of a deduction; (iv) advance pricing agreements and mutual agreement procedures with the ETA Transfer Pricing unit (Ministerial Decree 661/2018); (v) intercompany dividend participation relief for dividends received from resident companies subject to normal Egyptian tax. BEPS Action 2 hybrid-mismatch rules have not been enacted; ETA may apply the statutory general anti-avoidance rule and transfer-pricing provisions to recharacterize hybrid instruments and artificial structures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT – Value Added Tax under Law 67 of 2016 (replacing the former General Sales Tax), administered by the Egyptian Tax Authority; customs import/export VAT is administered jointly with the Egyptian Customs Authority via the NAFIZA single window.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory VAT registration threshold: EGP 500,000 of annual taxable turnover or taxable supplies in the preceding 12 months; voluntary registration from EGP 100,000. Exporters and importers must register regardless of turnover, and registration is required before commencing taxable activity.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-registered taxpayers, including exporters, are onboarded to the ETA e-invoicing system. B2B invoices must be transmitted in real time to ETA using the unified XML/JSON schema via API or web portal; ETA validates the invoice and returns a unique UUID and 2D barcode/QR code without which the invoice is fiscally invalid and input VAT credit is denied. B2C transactions fall within the phased e-receipt system where applicable. No physical fiscal stamp or banderole applies to resin figurines, and no dedicated fiscal clearance hardware is required beyond ETA e-invoice validation; export invoices must be reconciled with NAFIZA export declarations and the matching FX receipt.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating (0%) applies to: (a) goods physically exported outside Egypt by a VAT-registered exporter under a NAFIZA customs export declaration, with title passing to a non-resident buyer and payment received in foreign currency through Egyptian banking channels; and (b) exported or offshore services rendered to a non-resident for effect and use wholly outside Egypt, with remuneration received in convertible currency. Conditions: the goods must leave Egypt or the services must be consumed abroad no later than 180 days from the date of the invoice or supply; the exporter must hold a valid tax card and exporter code; failure to satisfy the export or repatriation timeline retroactively converts the zero rating to 14% output VAT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: NAFIZA Customs Export Declaration (بيان جمركي تصديري) stamped by the Egyptian Customs Authority
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical shipment to the foreign buyer
Inward Remittance Certificate or FX bank credit advice from an Egyptian licensed bank evidencing receipt of the foreign-currency export proceeds
Sales contract or non-resident purchase order
Exporter registration certificate and VAT tax card extract
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA cross-checks e-invoices, NAFIZA export declarations, bank FX receipts and CBE exchange-control records. If zero-rated goods are not exported within the 180-day window, or export proceeds are not repatriated through Egyptian banks within the Central Bank of Egypt deadline, ETA claws back the zero rating and assesses 14% output VAT plus monthly delay penalties and statutory interest from the original invoice date. Fraudulent claims, such as false export declarations, fictitious inward remittances, or re-importation of exported goods, attract criminal penalties under VAT Law 67/2016, including imprisonment and fines of not less than 100% and not exceeding 200% of the tax evaded, mandatory repayment of any refunded VAT, revocation of the VAT/Tax Card, and NAFIZA/GOEIC blacklisting of the exporter and its responsible officers.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) – General Department for Foreign Exchange Supervision and the Foreign Exchange Committee
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a managed-float regime under Law No. 194 of 2020. Current-account transactions for genuine trade and service payments are generally settled at the interbank market rate without a prior surrender requirement, but each transaction must pass through an authorized bank. Capital-account transactions, including share capital injections, capital increases by non-residents, and subsequent divestment or dividend remittances, are technically permitted but are subject to a documentary evidence chain and CBE/GAFI validation. Dividend and branch profit remittance is allowed to the extent that the LLC meets annual audit, tax clearance, Central Vigilance Organization reporting, and supports the outgoing transfer with the original inward MT103 or central bank foreign-exchange receipt. Full free convertibility is absent because non-resident funds may be directed into a special ‘private free account’ or temporarily held in local foreign-currency accounts, but any conversion to EGP or remittance triggers bank-level compliance, CBE daily reporting, and in practice the bank may require an underlying hedge-eligible trade or investment transaction document. Profit remittance hurdles include: outstanding tax balances, pending value-added-tax filings, absence of audited financial statements, or mismatched legal form/goods descriptions in the custom duties declaration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Pursuant to CBE General Rules for Foreign Exchange Business issued under Law 194/2020, export proceeds must be repatriated to an Egyptian licensed commercial bank and credited to the exporter’s account within 180 days from the date of the bill of lading, airway bill, or equivalent transport document. The mandatory conversion ratio is 50% of the foreign-currency export proceeds, which must be immediately converted to EGP at the prevailing interbank rate; the remaining 50% may be retained in a foreign-currency account for working-capital purposes, imports, or debt-service obligations. Exemptions apply only where the exporter holds an authorized import financing allocation, a CBE approved offsetting foreign-currency liability schedule, or the export arises from a duty-free / free-zone operation with separate CBE FX authorisation. Failure to repatriate within the statutory window exposes the LLC to CBE penalties, limitation of bank credit lines, and an automatic reconciliation order against the proceeds.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary clearing rail and Medium as an ancillary collection gateway. Egyptian law and CBE regulations recognize only licensed Egyptian banks and licensed exchange houses as authorized deposit-taking and FX transaction entities. Offshore digital EMI accounts (Wise, Payoneer, Revolut Business, or similar) are not permissible as the statutory receiving account for export proceeds or for settlement of inbound equity capital, because such accounts are not within CBE supervision and do not produce the documentary chain required for Egyptian tax and foreign-exchange clearance. The practical use case is limited to enabling overseas pre-order deposits and PayPal/Stripe payouts, provided the LLC maintains full visibility of the ultimate account holder and routes surplus balances through a licensed correspondent bank into an Egyptian bank account within 90 calendar days. For statutory export and treasury purposes, a bank-held foreign-currency account in Egypt is mandatory.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of at least one director or a senior manager holding a valid commercial power of attorney is generally required at the designated bank branch for the account-opening KYC interview. Remote onboarding is not recognized as a full alternative for Egyptian corporate accounts by CBE’s customer-due-diligence circulars. In practice, the authorized director or appointed Egyptian resident representative must attend the initial meeting; the remaining beneficial owners may satisfy the bank using authenticated passports, board resolutions, and notarized/vetted ownership charts, but at least one physical appearance at the commercial-account opening desk remains mandatory for the signatory and account applicant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Multi-layered beneficial-ownership structure with non-Egyptian intermediate companies or trusts in the LLC ownership chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide an audited corporate diagram extending to each ultimate natural-person shareholder; authenticated certificate of incorporation, registry commercial extracts, articles of association, and beneficial-ownership declarations for every intermediate entity; apostilled or consular-certified translations into Arabic; and a GAFI investor profile card reflecting the full chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-face-to-face identity of very risky signatory or unexplained source of funds for share-capital subscription.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit originals or certified copies of each passport and national-ID card of UBOs, board resolution authorizing fund subscription and signatory powers, dated KYC questionnaire, source-of-wealth statement, and bank reference letters from the remitting foreign bank; include audited financial statements or buy-side agreements supporting the liquidity used for the capital contribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear economic purpose or mismatch between ISIC 3240 commercial description and large inbound capital amount relative to stated production capacity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a scaled business plan, order book invoice/purchase orders from overseas distributors, rent or ownership lease for the resin casting facility, hardware procurement contracts for vacuum-casting machines, moulds, paints and resins, and photographs or a video tour of the production floor; align the bank introduction with a formal corporate authorization letter naming the signatory and an explanation of order-to-sale cash-flow coverage.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential exposure to politically exposed persons, sanctions, or named-party screening where the foreign customer is a US/EU buyer but the funds path passes through a Gulf intermediate bank.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain negative-media and sanctions screening reports for every customer and director; include an OFAC/UN/EU-list certificate and written declaration that the funds derive only from legitimate retail sales of licensed art collectibles; attach the distribution agreement, commercial invoice, customs tariff classification, bill of lading, and shipping insurance certificate; if the full wire path is through Bahrain/UAE, add the correspondent intermediary’s compliance release note and an updated enhanced-due-diligence company questionnaire.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The non-resident member initiates the capital injection by SWIFT MT103 from a bank outside Egypt to the LLC's authorized Egyptian bank foreign-currency account, remitting exactly USD/EUR to the entity and using a purpose code that aligns with equity injection into an Egyptian limited liability company, such as “Direct Investment – Equity Capital” under the CBE’s daily balance reporting codes. The receiving Egyptian bank applies a two-step control: first it matches the inward transfer to the LLC’s GoV/Registry credentials, an entry from the General Authority for Investment (GAFI) certificate, and the banking signature card; second it obtains a copy of the capital-declaration statement and records the purpose under CBE’s electronic reporting system. If the remittance exceeds an administrative threshold (generally USD 100,000 or its equivalent), the bank must request proof of the underlying GAFI registration contract, articles of association certified by the commercial registry, and the shareholders' resolution approving the increased capitalization. Funds may be retained as foreign currency in the LLC’s FCA or converted to EGP for factory overheads only after the bank processes a standard currency conversion with a Form E-B statement; the transaction must be reported to the CBE under the

stage_4.outbound_trade_disbursements: For operating disbursements and import of resin, pigments, moulding rubber, and packaging materials, the LLC may use: (i) direct SWIFT MT103/202 payments to foreign suppliers under open-account terms with a credit-insured facility; (ii) documentary letters of credit issued at Egypt banks under UCP600, where the issuing bank sends MT700/MT707 to the beneficiary’s bank; (iii) documentary collections against acceptance (D/A) or payment (D/P) under URC 522. Commercial LCs are particularly suitable for high-value resin production machinery and mould tooling. The Egyptian bank will require the import invoice, bill of lading, certificate of origin, and the customs import ledger for conversion of EGP to FX; after receipt of the goods, the LLC must file the Egyptian customs declaration and support the bank with the supplier’s final invoice and receipted proof for the foreign remittance. All outward FX settlements must be made at interbank rates and cannot be structured to circumvent CBE trade-control timelines; amounts above USD 200,000 may trigger additional bank-level treasury scrutiny and an extended documentary hold.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Delivered USD/EGP forward contracts with a licensed Egyptian bank, supported by underlying invoicing commitments, export revenues, or import payment schedules; typical tenor ranges from 1 to 12 months.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) USD/EGP contracts, entered into by the Egyptian bank on behalf of the LLC using CBE-reported interbank EGP rates for fixing, with cash settlement in USD/EGP at maturity and permitted only when supported by verified trade exposure.

Cross-currency swap agreements (EGP principal against USD principal) between the LLC and an authorized Egyptian bank, used solely for hedging a confirmed capital-remittance, long-term investment, or monetary obligation that is documented through cash-flow projections and board-approved treasury authorization.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Form 1) with audited financial statements and supporting tax schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - corporate tax district of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months of the close of the tax period; for a calendar-year LLC, on or before April 30 of the following year (Law No. 91/2005, Art. 31)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 2% cumulative monthly delay surcharge on unpaid tax; discretionary assessment if the return is over 60 days late; denial of the annual tax clearance certificate required for commercial register renewal; forced collection in persistent default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual partners' general meeting approving audited financial statements and the auditor's report, with minutes recorded in the statutory minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Partners' assembly of the LLC; records retained at the registered office and submitted to ETA with the corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the financial year-end (Companies Law No. 159/1981, Art. 41)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines on managers under Law No. 159/1981; unapproved accounts render the tax return incomplete and result in withholding of the ETA tax clearance certificate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual commercial register certificate renewal and fee payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI Commercial Register Office, Ministry of Trade and Industry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due annually by January 31, with the renewal window opening on January 1; registrations may renew on the registration anniversary if originally filed mid-year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-renewal fine after January 31; failure to renew beyond 60 days triggers administrative suspension of the commercial record and administrative strike-off, rendering the LLC legally incapable of concluding commercial acts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of the Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI Commercial Register; data accessible to the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (Egyptian FIU)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed with the annual commercial register renewal on or before January 31; any UBO or shareholding change is separately disclosed within 15 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines under Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 80/2002 as amended; suspension of the commercial record and refusal of the annual renewal until the declaration is filed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual insured payroll statement and social insurance declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI) - local insurance office of the factory district
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before January 31 following the reporting calendar year; monthly social insurance contributions remain due by the 15th of the following month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 2% monthly surcharge on unpaid contributions; criminal fines for deliberate misdeclaration; blockage of the GAFI annual renewal certificate in repeated default cases.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: December/calendar-year closing VAT return and December salary withholding tax return (final periodic filing of the year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - VAT and withholding tax desks of the registered-office tax district
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before January 20 of the succeeding calendar year (Law No. 67/2016, monthly filing rule)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fine of EGP 2,000-5,000 per return plus 2% monthly delay surcharge; repeated omissions trigger a comprehensive ETA audit and refusal of the annual tax clearance certificate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual municipal industrial/trade operating license renewal and Chamber of Commerce subscription
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local municipal license office and the regional chamber of the Federation of Egyptian Chambers of Commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from January through March 31, per the local improvement-fund billing cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative closure of the resin casting workshop; non-renewal of the industrial operation permit; inclusion on the municipal defaulters' list, which blocks GAFI clearance for the commercial record.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory auditor is compulsory for an LLC whose issued capital exceeds EGP 50,000 (Companies Law No. 159/1981, Art. 82); audited financial statements must accompany the corporate income tax return under Law No. 91/2005, so every operating LLC, including small resin-casting workshops, must commission a certified audit annually.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS) issued by ministerial decree, substantially converged with IFRS; IFRS directly applicable for consolidated parent-group reporting and acceptable for foreign-investor SPVs presenting global accounts.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No automatic CIT holiday for a standard LLC. Preferential levers: (a) SME Law 152/2020 election: progressive revenue-based rates of 0.5% on the first EGP 500,000, 0.75% on the next tranche, and 1% up to EGP 2,000,000 annual revenue, subject to SME size/employee ceilings; (b) Investment Law 72/2017 licensed projects may deduct 30%-50% of qualifying capital investment from taxable profits for 5-7 years (SCZone/GAFI approval required); (c) free-zone profits taxed at 0% where the entity is validly licensed. For an ISIC 3240 small resin-manufacturing unit, the SME Law 152/2020 revenue-based rates are the primary effective-tax-rate lever, provided the entity files the statutory election and maintains e-invoice compliance.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 19 - Corporate Income Tax Return (Eitarad Darb Al-Dakhl) filed exclusively through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) unified e-Tax/iTax electronic portal (https://eta.gov.eg); audited financial statements and tax schedules are mandatory e-attachments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 4 months after the end of the fiscal year (Article 40, Law 91/2005); the fiscal year is the calendar year unless a different period is pre-approved by the ETA; the tax due must be paid with the return, and compliance with the e-invoice/e-receipt integration is verified at filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, ETA tax registration number (EIN), commercial register number, tax card number, legal form, and head office address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident-owned LLC must hold a valid Egyptian EIN and commercial registry extract; enter the ETA-issued EIN exactly as registered; appoint a resident tax agent for service of process where the ETA requires one.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Start and end dates of the tax period covered by the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Align with the approved fiscal year; a non-calendar year requires prior ETA approval evidenced in writing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Description of the principal business activity and the corresponding ISIC activity code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use ISIC 3240 (Manufacture of games and toys) / NAICS 339930 for polyresin vacuum-cast statues; the code must match the commercial license, otherwise the return is treated as inconsistent and selected for inspection.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total worldwide gross revenues, including export sales, domestic sales, pre-order deposits, and all payment-rail inflows (Stripe, PayPal, bank transfers), translated into EGP at the prevailing official bank rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile declared revenue to e-invoice records and payment gateway statements; unreported foreign-currency inflows are treated as tax evasion; apply the arm's-length principle for any intercompany sales.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Raw materials (resin, pigments, molds), direct labor, and production overhead properly supported by inventory records and purchase invoices.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Related-party purchases of resin or molds must be documented under Egypt's TP rules; provide a schedule reconciling COGS to audited financial statements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Depreciation, amortization, wages, marketing, and other deductible operating expenditures as permitted by the Executive Regulations of Law 91/2005.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-deductible items must be added back: 50% cap on entertainment, charitable donations subject to caps, 30% EBITDA interest limitation and 4:1 debt-to-equity thin-cap rule; no deduction for unsubstantiated management fees paid to offshore affiliates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount of prior-year tax losses applied against current-year taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses assessed within the prior 5 years and evidenced by ETA loss certificates may be deducted; non-resident shareholders cannot personally use the LLC's losses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit before tax adjusted for statutory add-backs and deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure that the audited financial statements, in EGP, tie to the return; any DTA-based exemption or treaty claim must be referenced in the notes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of the 22.5% CIT rate, or the SME Law 152/2020 progressive revenue-based rates if the election was validly made.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a foreign-owned LLC, the SME election remains available only if ownership, revenue, and headcount tests are met and the activity is not disqualified; misusing the SME rate is a fraud red flag.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits, prepaid taxes, quarterly advance installments, and any final withholding previously settled.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach foreign tax credit certificates and bank evidence of advance payments; treaty-country TRCs must be attached if reduced dividend/interest/royalty WHT was applied.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a fixed fine of EGP 5,000 - EGP 50,000 plus a monthly delay surcharge of 2% of the unpaid tax (capped at 80%) under Law 91/2005 as reinforced by the Unified Tax Procedures Law 67/2023; non-filing can void loss carry-forwards, trigger a desk audit, automatic assessment, and criminal referral; electronic filing failures are separately fined up to EGP 100,000.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quarterly CIT advance installment payment voucher - ETA e-Tax/iTax portal e-payment module.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Installments are due by the end of March, June, September, and December of the tax year; each installment equals 25% of the pro-rata prior-year assessed CIT liability; no separate return is filed at installment dates, but payment receipts must be reconciled in the annual Form No. 19.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarter number and fiscal year to which the advance payment relates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the prior-year assessed tax as the base; first-year entities pay on estimated tax with ETA acceptance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 25% of prior-year assessed tax for each quarter.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment must be funded from the Egyptian bank account of the LLC; third-party payments trigger anti-money-laundering reviews.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: ETA-issued electronic receipt number for each installment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain receipts for a minimum of 5 years; missing receipts create a presumption of non-payment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Non-payment of quarterly installments triggers a 2% monthly surcharge on the shortfall (capped at 80%) and accelerates the enforcement of the annual tax debt, including bank attachment and travel-ban procedures.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding tax on dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders under Article 56, Law 91/2005 as amended; resident corporate shareholders may claim a participation exemption where statutory conditions are met.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief: (1) obtain the home-jurisdiction Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) covering the year of distribution, signed and legalized as required; (2) execute the ETA WHT relief application form with a beneficial-ownership declaration; (3) submit the TRC and holding-period evidence (e.g., 25%+ capital for the reduced 5% rate, if applicable) to the paying LLC before the dividend payment date; (4) the Egyptian LLC applies the treaty rate only after obtaining ETA pre-approval where the relevant DTA requires it, and otherwise withholds at the statutory 10% and files for refund; (5) retain TRCs and distribution board minutes for 5 years for audit.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 20% WHT on royalties paid to non-residents for patents, trademarks, know-how, and similar intangibles; 20% WHT on interest paid to non-resident lenders. Treaty rates commonly reduce interest to 10%-15% and royalties to 10%-20% (rates vary by DTA). Law 26/2020 thin-cap rules further cap interest deductibility at 30% of EBITDA for related-party debt exceeding a 4:1 debt-to-equity ratio; interest on shareholder loans is scrutinized against substance and arm's-length criteria.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 15,000,000 aggregate annual related-party transactions: crossing this threshold mandates attaching TP disclosure forms TP-1/TP-2 to the Form No. 19 return and maintaining contemporaneous documentation. Master File and Local File obligations apply for multinational groups with consolidated group revenue of at least EGP 3,000,000,000; the ETA may demand TP documentation below the threshold where transactions involve low-tax jurisdictions or a foreign shareholder without substance.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not operate a standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) statute comparable to UAE/Caribbean regimes. Instead, the ETA applies substance-over-form doctrines, the beneficial-ownership tests embedded in Egypt's DTA network, CFC rules introduced by Law 26/2020, and GAAR anti-abuse principles. An ISIC 3240 resin-statue LLC must maintain verifiable economic substance: physical production premises, resin/mold inventories, Egyptian payroll for casting and painting staff, export/import customs records, and board minutes of actual management meetings in Egypt. A passive 'letterbox' LLC claiming treaty benefits while acting as a conduit for foreign shareholders will be denied DTA relief, face deemed-PE attribution, and risk having its limited-liability shield pierced.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling polyresin statues through PayPal/Stripe pre-order channels without issuing e-invoices, omitting foreign-currency receipts from the CIT return, maintaining dual sets of sales books, or falsifying inventory counts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment of 2-5 years plus a fine equal to 100%-200% of the evaded tax under Law 91/2005 and Unified Tax Procedures Law 67/2023; automatic upward assessment; mandatory confiscation of production equipment; immediate loss of all SME preferential rates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and authorised managers are jointly and severally liable for unpaid taxes and withheld amounts; criminal conviction triggers asset seizure, travel bans, bank-account freezes, and disqualification from serving on boards of Egyptian companies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to attach TP-1/TP-2 when related-party transactions cross the EGP 15,000,000 threshold, or applying non-arm's-length markups on resin raw materials sourced from a related foreign supplier without contemporaneous comparability analysis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CIT adjustment by the ETA using TNMM or profit split with an uplift penalty of 30% of the additional tax; separate fixed fines under the 2020 amendments; listing on the ETA non-compliant taxpayer register; reversal of underlying expense deductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors signing knowingly false TP declarations are personally liable for the penal uplift and are exposed to criminal referral for filing false tax documents.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Recording shareholder withdrawals or unsecured shareholder loans as receivables without interest, repayment, or board authorization; funding a foreign affiliate's marketing costs from Egypt without charging arm's-length remuneration or applying WHT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of outstanding balances as deemed dividend distributions subject to 10% WHT plus a 2% monthly delay surcharge (capped at 80%); CFC attribution of passive income; interest disallowance under thin-cap rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managing directors are statutorily required to withhold 10% dividend WHT at the time of payment; failure to withhold creates personal liability for the full withheld amount, interest, and penalties, enforceable through personal bank attachment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Structure / Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Employing a Cyprus, UAE, or free-zone mailbox entity to invoice the Egyptian LLC for non-existent R&D, design, or marketing services without staff, premises, or records; claiming DTA benefits where beneficial ownership is absent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits and recharacterization of payments as taxable dividends or services; 20% WHT imposed on the gross amount; CFC taxation on shifted profits; the foreign entity may be delisted from the Egyptian commercial registry and the Egyptian LLC's deductions are reversed with evasion penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of both the Egyptian LLC and the foreign shell face criminal fraud liability under the Egyptian Penal Code and AML Law; Egyptian travel bans are routinely issued in collection proceedings; corporate veil piercing is available where the LLC is operated as an instrument of fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing business receipts through personal PayPal/Stripe accounts not linked to the commercial registry, structuring cash inflows to fall below reporting thresholds, or accepting recurring cross-border pre-order payments from high-risk jurisdictions without customer due diligence records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AML Law 80/2002 as amended: imprisonment of 3-7 years and a fine of EGP 50,000-1,000,000 for natural persons; for legal persons, fines up to EGP 2,000,000 plus confiscation; the ETA treats unreported payment-rail inflows as deemed revenues subject to full evasion penalties and 22.5% CIT on the entire amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors knowingly executing or benefitting from unreported payment rails are prosecuted as principals; bank accounts are frozen, corporate e-invoice permits are suspended, travel bans are issued, and directors are barred from re-licensing business activities in Egypt.
